title: Finite negative-square census and conductor-commutator gate

verdict.conclusion: The reflection form gives an exact integer negative-square census for distinct off-line mirror cycles and remains indefinite arbitrarily near the line or high in the strip.  Pullback through finite interpolation preserves this inertia.  For zeta, however, the same completed form is the Weil form; proving zero index from its prime side is RH-equivalent.  Local conductor commutators do not assemble into an established independently computable global Fredholm index.

finiteTheorem.fullQuartet: one off-line quartet has two mirror 2-cycles and inertia (2,2,0)
finiteTheorem.interpolation: for distinct nodes, polynomial evaluation is an invertible Vandermonde map V; G=V*JV is congruent to J and has the same inertia

arithmeticPromotionGates.detail: the Guinand--Weil explicit formula equates the zero reflection form with pole, gamma and prime-power terms on its legitimate test domain
proving that this completed form has no negative square for every admissible test is Weil positivity, which is equivalent to RH
multiplicity rescales a mirror block but does not add independent negative directions; a confluent derivative-jet lift has no established prime-side realization
finite bandwidth restricts interpolation, while removing the window restores the complete RH-equivalent Weil test space

conductorCommutatorGates.outcome: fails to imply the completed sign
conductorCommutatorGates.detail: Burnol's nonnegative local time-delay symbol enters the conductor as log(p)-tau_p; the conductor contribution is signed
the local explicit formula is represented by a supertrace plus an identity correction, not by an ordinary positive trace
no canonical completed pair of projections with compact difference is supplied by the local formulae; the unsmoothed sum over places requires the same global regularisation as the explicit formula
an index extracted from the phase of xi is the argument-principle zero count, while no place-by-place prime calculation proving zero index is known
the finite negative-square census succeeds as a detector, but neither the Weil prime side nor the conductor commutators provide an independent exclusion engine

sonineReflectionGate.establishedInput: Burnol's zero systems are complete and minimal with canonical biorthogonal data
sonineReflectionGate.verdict: a positive reflection metric would have to eliminate exactly this negative block; completeness alone does not do so, and no arithmetic positivity theorem weaker than Weil positivity was found

stopRuleApplied: the route was stopped because the only completed prime-side sign is Weil positivity and the proposed global conductor index is not defined by the established local theory
minimalMissingObject: a completion-native Fredholm pair or homotopy whose index is forced by an off-line mirror cycle and can be computed as zero from primes, pole and gamma terms without invoking zero locations or Weil positivity
status: quantized detection proved; independent arithmetic exclusion not found; RH remains open
